title: Triple Stellar Treat
caption: The triple star system HP Tau, imaged by the Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope
celestial: HP Tau · constellation Taurus · about 550 light-years away (source figure)
credit: KPNO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab). Image processing: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage/NSF NOIRLab), M. Zamani (NSF NOIRLab) & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Three stars sit at the centre of this image, wrapped in a large arcing reflection nebula. They form a triple star system that includes HP Tau, a variable star in Taurus that lies more than 550 light-years away.

HP Tau belongs to the T Tauri class of young, unruly stars that are easing into a calmer phase of life called the main sequence. How long a star stays on the main sequence depends on its mass. The Sun, for example, is about halfway through its main-sequence lifetime of roughly 10 billion years.

The surrounding nebula shines by reflection rather than emission. Its dust reflects light from nearby stars instead of glowing on its own, the way emission nebulae elsewhere in the Universe do. The image was made from data gathered by Kitt Peak National Observatory's Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (20.83 x 11.77 arcminutes) and distance (550 light years), the frame spans roughly 3.3 × 1.9 light-years. Its light set out about 550 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Taken with the Mosaic I camera on the NSF Nicholas U. Mayall 4-meter Telescope through g, r and i filters. The colour mapping isn't published.
